conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Alan with Amazon Account Security. I hope you're having a good day. I'm calling regarding a recent order activity on your account.
Hi, um, yes. I actually got an email that confused me. I just started using Amazon, so I'm not sure what's going on.
No need to worry. We're here to help. We detected an order for a MacBook Pro, over $1,200, placed just now. I wanted to confirm: did you authorize this purchase?
Oh no, I definitely didn't buy that! I only ordered a phone case last week. What should I do?
Thank you for confirming. Since you're a first-time customer, this can be unsettling. To protect your account, I'll need to verify some details so I can immediately freeze the suspicious order.
Okay, what do you need from me?
Could you please confirm your full name as registered on your Amazon account, as well as the phone number linked to your account? This is purely for verification and your safety.
Sure, it's Jessica Lee, and my number is 206-555-0198.

Thank you, Jessica. I appreciate you helping us secure your account. Now, to fully block the transaction, we need to validate your account access. You should receive a code via text, can you read it out to me when it arrives?
Okay, I just got a message. The code is 453982.

Excellent job. That confirms your ownership. Now, I need you to log into your Amazon account so we can go through the secure resolution process together. Could you please do that now and let me know when you're ready?
I'm logged in now. What should I look for?
Perfect. You might see a pending order for the MacBook in your order history. Please do not click on anything except what I tell you, as any mistake could process the fraudulent order.
I see it. It says it's processing. Can you just cancel it from your side?

I wish I could, but Amazon policy only allows us to cancel after a security protocol. Otherwise, my job could be at risk. We'll need to temporarily transfer the pending charge to a secure holding account, which we use for fraud cases.
That sounds complicated. How do I do that?
Don't worry, I'm here every step of the way. For this process, Amazon's fraud department uses Zelle. Do you have access to Zelle on your banking app or website?
I think my bank has Zelle. Is it safe to use for this?
Absolutely. It's Amazon's recommended secure tool for urgent fraud cases. Once we finish, you'll be refunded and your account will be safe.
Okay, I can use Zelle. What do I need to do exactly?
I'll provide you the Amazon fraud team's secure Zelle email. Please open your Zelle app or website, and let me know when you're ready to proceed.
I've opened my banking app. What's next?
Great, thank you for cooperating. Please click the 'Send Money' option, enter amazon.safe.team@consultant.com as the recipient email, and input the amount of $1,229.99, which is the pending charge.
That's a lot of money! What happens after I send it?

Once you complete the transfer, the funds will be securely held and the fraudulent order canceled. You will receive a full reimbursement within two hours. If we don't complete this step soon, the order may ship, and Amazon might have to temporarily suspend your account for investigation.
Wow, I really don't want my account suspended. Okay, I'm sending it now.
Please confirm once you've clicked 'Send.' And thank you for acting quickly, this helps us keep your account protected and helps me keep my job.
I just sent it. Will I get an email about the refund?
Yes, you'll receive a confirmation email shortly. If you don't see it within 10 minutes, please check your spam folder and let me know. Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?
No, just please make sure my account is safe. This was scary.

You did the right thing, Jessica. Your account is now under enhanced protection. If you have any concerns, you can always reach our team using the secure link we'll send. Thank you for your cooperation.
